sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test imports
sections.what: Brings in the test runner, the assertion helper, the metric calculations and the assertion schema that the tests need.
sections.why: Likely reason: each test uses these pieces, and the fact builder needs the schema.

sections.name: fact
sections.title: Builds a made-up test fact
sections.what: Creates a fictional project fact with a field, value, source link and a passing assessment, so the metric tests can run on fixed inputs.
sections.why: The comment says these tests check arithmetic and lineage, not whether a source is true.
sections.watch_out: The source link is fake, so a passing test says nothing about real project data.

sections.name: money
sections.title: Tests cost, date and withholding rules
sections.what: Checks three groups of cases: a zero change keeps its input trail; conflicting, mismatched or forecast records produce no cost result; dates keep their precision and mismatched or cancelled outcomes produce no schedule result. Also checks that invalid dates and ambiguous numbers are refused.
sections.why: Likely reason: these are the cases where a wrong number would most easily reach a report.
sections.watch_out: Expected results are fixed, so an intended rule change will fail these tests until they are updated.

summary: Automated tests that check the project cost and schedule calculations use only admitted, consistent facts and withhold results when the facts do not support one.
purpose: Proves the calculation rules behave as designed before the metrics are trusted in a report.
why: Likely reason: wrong cost or schedule numbers would be the most damaging errors in the output, so each withholding rule has a test.
how: Builds made-up project facts with fixed values, runs the metric calculation on them, and checks the expected results. Also checks that invalid dates and ambiguous numbers are rejected.
inputs: Synthetic project facts created inside the file. No real project data is read.
outputs: Pass or fail results for each test group.
risks: The facts are invented, so a passing test shows the arithmetic and rules work, not that the real sources are correct.
debug: If a test fails, read the failing assertion first, then check the matching rule in the metrics file. If the rule changed on purpose, update the expected result here too.
